title: The Return of the German Question
gist: Teaser: Joschka Fischer warns that the AfD's 43.8% in the September 6 Saxony-Anhalt election puts an openly ethnonationalist party near government power for the first time in the Federal Republic, and with pro-Russian forces rising in France, Europeans must prepare for the worst.

insights.claim: On September 6, the far-right Alternative für Deutschland won 43.8% of the vote in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt, falling just short of an absolute majority.
insights.speaker: JOSCHKA FISCHER
insights.so_what: A near-majority far-right result is a material shift in German political risk.
insights.quote: won 43.8% of the vote in the German federal state of Saxony-Anhalt, falling just short of an absolute majority

insights.claim: For the first time since the founding of the Federal Republic, an openly ethnonationalist party with a platform ideologically adjacent to National Socialism is close to gaining government power.
insights.speaker: JOSCHKA FISCHER
insights.so_what: AfD in government at state level could challenge German policy consensus on Europe and Russia.
insights.quote: For the first time since the founding of the Federal Republic, an openly ethnonationalist (indeed, racist) party

insights.claim: With similarly pro-Russian forces rising in France alongside the AfD in Germany, Europeans must prepare for a worst-case scenario affecting the EU's core.
insights.speaker: JOSCHKA FISCHER
insights.so_what: Simultaneous pro-Russian gains in Germany and France threaten EU cohesion, Ukraine support and sanctions policy; a tail risk for European assets.
insights.quote: with similarly pro-Russian forces on the rise in France, all Europeans must prepare for the worst
